subtitle: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <cstddef> header. SHIPPED 2026-08-25. All 11 catalogued symbols across 7 granular headers plus the umbrella. The module is two different things at once, and the split is the interesting part: size_t / ptrdiff_t / nullptr_t / max_align_t are implementation-fixed and can only be re-exported (identity preserved), while byte / to_integer / the eleven byte operators are ordinary C++ that re_std owns outright and back-ports from C++17 to C++11 -- a six-year lead. offsetof and NULL are macros and have no re_std:: spelling at all. One language ceiling is recorded rather than worked around: byte{0x2A} needs P0138R2 (C++17), so C++11/14 callers write static_cast<byte>(n).
legend_blurb: <cstddef> provides the fundamental typedefs (size_t, ptrdiff_t, nullptr_t, max_align_t) and the byte type for raw storage.

symbols.name: size_t
symbols.notes: Identity-preserving re-export of std::size_t. The result type of sizeof is an ABI fact -- unsigned long on LP64, unsigned long long on Windows -- so it can only be surfaced, never defined. Preserving identity means a value binds to either spelling and picks the same overload.

symbols.name: ptrdiff_t
symbols.notes: Identity-preserving re-export of std::ptrdiff_t, the signed result of subtracting two pointers. Same reasoning as size_t.

symbols.name: nullptr_t
symbols.notes: Identity-preserving re-export of std::nullptr_t. It is decltype(nullptr), a compiler-synthesised type whose conversion rules live in the language. A hand-rolled empty struct would not be the type a bare nullptr has, so overloads taking it would never be selected by an actual null pointer literal.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 language floor: decltype(nullptr) cannot be formed before C++11. Gated out below that tier rather than substituting a NULL-shaped stand-in with different conversion rules.

symbols.name: max_align_t
symbols.notes: Re-export of std::max_align_t on the primary path. Where <cstddef> declares none (libstdc++ before GCC 4.9, some freestanding libraries), re_std synthesises a union of the widest scalars -- correct on every ABI the authors know of, but a CONSTRUCTION rather than the implementation's own answer, so identity is NOT preserved on that path. D_RE_STD_HAS_STD_MAX_ALIGN_T reports which was taken.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor: the type does not exist in C++98.

symbols.name: byte
symbols.notes: RE_STD OWNS THIS TYPE -- not a re-export. An ordinary scoped enumeration over unsigned char with no compiler magic behind it, so re_std defines its own and back-ports it six years. The consequence is deliberate: on C++17+ re_std::byte and std::byte are DIFFERENT types and neither converts to the other. Re-exporting on C++17+ and defining below was rejected -- it would give one spelling two identities depending on tier, the exact failure mode the library exists to prevent. ONE SPELLING DOES NOT BACK-PORT: byte{0x2A} is P0138R2, a C++17 LANGUAGE change, so on C++11/14 construct with static_cast<byte>(n), which is constexpr at every tier. No to_byte() factory is provided -- std has no such function and inventing surface std lacks would break portability in the other direction.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor: the interface IS a scoped enumeration, which is a C++11 feature. An unscoped enum would convert to int, a class wrapper would not work in a switch or as a non-type template argument; either would be a different type from the standard's. Separately, direct-list-initialisation from an integer (byte{0x2A}) is bounded at C++17 by P0138R2 and cannot be back-ported -- a LANGUAGE ceiling, not a library one.

symbols.name: to_integer<IntType>
symbols.notes: The single documented exit from byte to the integers; the target type is explicit and never deduced. Constrained with enable_if rather than a static_assert so that to_integer<some_class>(b) is a SUBSTITUTION FAILURE -- it drops out of overload resolution quietly instead of hard-erroring and poisoning any surrounding detection idiom.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor: follows byte, whose interface is a scoped enumeration. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- a C++98 path via the struct-wrapper idiom the review checklist prescribes for enum class is possible and is tracked as planned work; it is not an unreachable tier.

symbols.name: operator<< / operator>> (byte, integer)
symbols.notes: Shifts, constrained to integer shift counts. The promotion trap is the whole implementation: the operand promotes to int before shifting, so bits pushed past position 7 survive in the promoted value and casting straight back to byte would be an out-of-range enum conversion. Every expression lands in unsigned char explicitly first. Same trap as hard-won rule 6, reached from the other direction.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor: follows byte, whose interface is a scoped enumeration. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- a C++98 path via the struct-wrapper idiom the review checklist prescribes for enum class is possible and is tracked as planned work; it is not an unreachable tier.

symbols.name: operator| & ^ ~ (byte)
symbols.notes: The four bitwise operations. Non-template free functions, so they carry D_CONSTEXPR_INLINE -- header-defined non-templates need inline or two translation units including the header is an ODR violation. operator~ masks to unsigned char to discard the high bits promotion produced.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor: follows byte, whose interface is a scoped enumeration. Floor question, not a coverage gap -- a C++98 path via the struct-wrapper idiom the review checklist prescribes for enum class is possible and is tracked as planned work; it is not an unreachable tier.

symbols.name: operator<<= >>= |= &= ^= (byte)
symbols.notes: The five compound assignments. Constexpr from C++14 rather than C++11 -- they mutate a reference parameter, which needs the relaxed C++14 rules -- and RE_STD IS AHEAD OF STD here, which made them constexpr in C++17. On C++11 they remain ordinary inline functions rather than being omitted. The explicit `inline` matters on that tier: with D_CONSTEXPR_CPP14 expanding to nothing, constexpr is no longer present to imply it.
symbols.failure_reason: C++11 floor: follows byte. The operations themselves are usable from C++11; they are constexpr only from C++14, since mutating a reference parameter needs the relaxed C++14 rules. Floor question, not a coverage gap.

symbols.name: offsetof
symbols.notes: Macro; Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability: the umbrella guarantees the macro is in scope, and the module fills it in from a compiler builtin where the platform's own header predates it. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden. Only defined behaviour on standard-layout types.

symbols.name: NULL
symbols.notes: Macro; Macros have no namespace, so there is no re_std:: spelling and none is invented. re_std's contribution is availability: the umbrella guarantees the macro is in scope, and the module fills it in from a compiler builtin where the platform's own header predates it. Every gap-fill is #ifndef-guarded -- a platform that answered is never overridden. Prefer D_NULLPTR or a bare nullptr: NULL is an integer literal in disguise and selects integer overloads.
